hypothesis: A scorer counter increase observed after recovery admission cannot be attributed to the recovery interval when the previous sample predates admission; requiring a post-admission, pre-input baseline and a bounded later positive sample rejects this ambiguity.
test: Five synthetic single-monotonic-clock cases; hidden event timing varies while scorer observations remain fixed in the ambiguity case.
decision_gate: PASS only if the identical observation histories with pre-admission vs recovery kill times classify as co-occurrence, the valid baseline + bounded-positive case qualifies, and missing baseline, excessive gap, missed poll, or invalid ordering fail closed.
missed_period_rule: Any missed scheduled scorer period rejects attribution.
clock_rule: All synthetic timestamps use one clock domain. A live integration must compare only timestamps converted through explicit same-domain host brackets; guest perf_counter_ns values must not be directly compared to host AppServer timestamps.
resources: CPU-only local deterministic test; no game, model, live input, GPU, Docker, or WSLc.
claim_limit: Admission-bracketed progress is still an observed interval association, not exact kill onset or causal proof that recovery caused progress.
